display.purpose: Overscale hero propositions; one emphasized line may carry Signal Green.

headline.purpose: Major section statements across dark, paper, and green fields.

title.purpose: Technology rows and strong local headings.

body.purpose: Readable explanatory copy held to controlled line lengths.

label.purpose: Uppercase action labels with operational tracking.

shadows.name: signal-glow
shadows.purpose: The functional glow around a six-pixel live-status node; no other component uses shadow.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Reciprocal color, border, icon, hover, selection, and compact control changes.

motion.name: large-state-transition
motion.purpose: Menus, overlays, accordions, and meaningful layout transitions in both directions.

motion.name: hero-line-reveal
motion.purpose: Introduces the two-line hero proposition from its clipped line masks without clipping descenders.

motion.name: hero-support-reveal
motion.purpose: Introduces hero copy, actions, and the visual field after the headline begins.

motion.name: section-reveal
motion.value: ScrollTrigger; 0.9s expo.out; y 24px max; opacity 0.15 to 1; 0.08–0.12s sibling stagger; trigger top 86%; once
motion.purpose: Reveals each section and its meaningful nested groups in reading order without fragmenting every text node.

motion.name: reversible-state-change
motion.value: subtle transition in both directions; state and focus update immediately
motion.purpose: Gives every visual state change an intentional return path without delaying interaction.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.purpose: Provides restrained smooth-wheel movement outside reduced-motion mode.

motion.name: hero-metal-shader
motion.value: continuous low-speed WebGL drift; speed 0.24; non-interactive; viewport and visibility paused
motion.purpose: Creates a cinematic infrastructure field behind the homepage proposition without decorative particles or camera zoom.

motion.name: capability-loop
motion.value: 2–3s concept-specific cycle; 3–6px translation; sine.inOut; viewport and visibility paused
motion.purpose: Explains preparation, resource selection, and separate data-channel rhythms without decorative motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transitions disabled; Lenis disabled; figure loops stopped; WebGL resolves to a static composition
motion.purpose: Preserves immediate content access and the complete visual relationship when motion is reduced.

narrative.overview:
The visual system treats cloud gaming as an operating network already in motion: a near-black control field, a single electric route signal, and cool paper surfaces that let corporate evidence read with editorial clarity. Its confidence comes from scale, alignment, and instrumentation rather than game-like spectacle.

The world is precise, spacious, and controlled. Overscale Archivo statements establish the proposition; compact Manrope labels behave like route annotations; rules, nodes, paths, indices, and cropped network frames make infrastructure visible without turning it into decorative sci-fi. Bright color is scarce and therefore meaningful.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black operations fields alternate with cool editorial paper and signal-green evidence bands.
Overscale, tightly tracked headlines are balanced by small uppercase manifest labels.
Thin rules, coordinate lines, circular nodes, cinematic shader ribbons, and isometric system figures visualize infrastructure.
Isometric figures use a few large three-tone objects; visible labels and routes appear only when the relationship cannot be understood without them.
Motion is smooth and low-amplitude, with a complete reduced-motion fallback.

rules.name: The Single Visual Source Rule
rules.body: Define a reusable visual decision once in DESIGN.md; other documents and code should reference or implement it rather than restating a competing version.

rules.name: The One Live Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Green is the only chromatic accent; its rarity identifies what is active, actionable, or operationally important.

rules.name: The Alternating Field Rule
rules.body: Move between Operational Ink, Editorial Paper, and full Signal Green sections to create rhythm; do not introduce extra surface colors.

rules.name: The Legible Pairing Rule
rules.body: Every text and essential-state color must use an approved surface pairing and pass the required contrast gate; color never carries state by itself.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Archivo speaks for propositions and structural titles; Manrope carries explanation, navigation, metadata, and actions.

rules.name: The Manifest Label Rule
rules.body: Small labels are uppercase, widely tracked, and concise; they annotate the system rather than compete with the message.

rules.name: The Instrument Grid Rule
rules.body: Every expressive element must still align to an edge, column, rule, node, or documented route; apparent freedom is held by a visible system.

rules.name: The Responsive Purpose Rule
rules.body: A breakpoint must resolve a real composition or usability change; components scale or reflow as complete systems instead of losing labels, paths, controls, or meaning.

rules.name: The Flat Infrastructure Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stay flat and square; use rules, fields, overlap, and route geometry before reaching for elevation.

rules.name: The Three-Face Depth Rule
rules.body: Every isometric block uses one hue family across three flat values: the top face is lightest, the left face is darkest, and the right face sits between them. Create depth through tonal faces and precise edges, never gradients or decorative drop shadows.

rules.name: The Node-or-Plane Rule
rules.body: Geometry is either a precise circular node or a sharp plane; avoid casual medium-radius cards and pill-shaped controls.

rules.name: The Operational Figure Rule
rules.body: A figure must communicate one real system idea through the fewest large, aligned shapes possible. Text and routes are optional evidence, not required decoration; the figure must never become a dense miniature schematic or generic futuristic ornament.

rules.name: The Evidence Before Atmosphere Rule
rules.body: Use imagery to clarify the company, technology, people, or operating context; atmosphere supports that evidence but never substitutes for it.

rules.name: The One Icon Family Rule
rules.body: Use Lucide for interface symbols; do not introduce another icon package, emoji, Unicode arrows, or one-off inline SVG controls unless the required brand or technical symbol does not exist in Lucide and the exception is documented.

rules.name: The Reversible Transition Rule
rules.body: If a visual element animates from state A to state B, its return from B to A must be equally intentional, subtle, and free of abrupt jumps.

rules.name: The Complete State Rule
rules.body: A component is complete only when its pointer, keyboard, active, reverse, disabled, error, and reduced-motion behavior have been considered and the applicable states are implemented.

rules.name: The Brand Mark Integrity Rule
rules.body: Choose the approved logo variant for contrast, preserve its geometry and clear space, and never treat the mark as a decorative background texture.

dos: Do reserve Signal Green for active routes, primary actions, focus, evidence fields, and a limited display emphasis.
Do use Archivo at decisive scale and Manrope for all explanatory and operational copy.
Do build hierarchy with spacing, thin rules, alignment, and alternating fields before adding decoration.
Do keep motion controlled: 250ms state transitions, 0.9–1.15s reveal sequences, and slow low-amplitude route movement.
Do provide reciprocal transitions for every reversible visual state and verify both directions, including menu close, accordion collapse, hover exit, inactive selection, and dismissed feedback.
Do preserve the implemented 900px, 620px, and 520px responsive transitions and the reduced-motion static fallback.
Do apply the Three-Face Depth Rule and Operational Figure Rule whenever creating or revising figures, shapes, system maps, or technical diagrams.
Do keep figures visually large and use the minimum number of vector parts needed to express one idea.
Do use SVG titles and descriptions when a figure is intentionally textless.
Do use only the approved logo assets and select the black or white variant according to surface contrast.
Do define every applicable component state and test pointer, keyboard, reverse, error, disabled, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do crop and optimize imagery for each responsive composition while preserving a quiet region for overlaid copy.
Do update DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json together whenever the reusable visual system changes.
Do keep page copy, implementation, and the matching content/pages brief synchronized in the same change.
donts: Don't add neon gradients, glowing orbs, glass cards, or game-interface chrome; the network itself is the visual metaphor.
Don't introduce rounded card systems or pill buttons into the sharp-plane and circular-node language.
Don't use Signal Green as ambient decoration across an entire composition; it must retain operational meaning.
Don't add decorative shadows to sections, cards, or actions.
Don't let animation delay access to content or survive a reduced-motion preference.
Don't use transition: all, delay keyboard focus, or animate only the entrance while leaving the reverse state abrupt.
Don't shrink figures into dense mini-schematics or add labels and routes merely to make them look technical.
Don't use flat single-value boxes, floating labels, incomplete paths, gradients, or decorative particles in operational figures.
Don't repeat the homepage shader as a generic background on unrelated sections.
Don't use placeholders as field labels, remove visible focus, or communicate an error or selected state through color alone.
Don't stretch, recolor, crop, shadow, rotate, or use the TGC logo as an ambient footer or section background.
Don't add generic gaming, crypto, neon-server, or futuristic imagery that does not add evidence about the adjacent section.
Don't create a competing visual-system rule in another document; link back to this file and update the canonical rule here.
